newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold looks again to break resistance.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold looks again to break resistance.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
LONODON, July 29 (REUTER) - Gold's close above $328.00 per ounce on Monday suggests a breakout is being attempted and could lead to a test of $335.70 per ounce, analysts said.
But first a fourth attempt at breaking the $329/$330 resistance would have to be successful, they added.
GOLD -
The push on $328.00 per ounce yesterday has given some hope that gold is finally going to make a bid to break from its established narrow confines, analysts said.
But first it had to succeed at the fourth time of asking to overcome resistance at $329/$330.
"There is a seven-month downtrend line at $335.70 which I expect it could find," said technical analyst Karen Jones at Credit Suisse First Boston.
There was nothing significant to stop gold between the initial resistance and the downtrend obstacle, she said, but that would be about the limit of gold's ambitions for now.
Support the mid-$330s resistance was a 63-day moving average and lows going back to February and April.
"That is going to be tough to beat," Jones said.
At 0740 GMT gold was indicated at $327.75/$328.05 down from a late close of $328.25/$328.75.
SILVER
After spending most of July moving sideways silver could be stirring along with gold, analysts said.
It has failed to sustain inroads to $4.40/$4.45 several times but Jones said there was a possibility now that silver was trying to correct further.
If so, it would find $4.59/$4.60 heavy resistance.
The silver-gold ratio had tested and failed at a seven-year downtrend of 77/76 last week.
Now a move from 75.20 (on Friday) could bring the ratio back to 73.50/73.00.
At 0740 GMT silver was indicated at $.37/$4/39 unchanged from Monday's late close.
PLATINUM
There was a chance that a still bullish platinum market could climb back to the early July peak at $437.00
"There is a sharp uptrend at $420 and scope is intact if that holds," said Jones.
Above $437 suggested an advance to $460.
The platinum-gold spread was back around $100 and if it got through $102, then the way was cleared to test resistance at $112-$117, Jones said.
At 0740 GMT platinum was indicated at $426.00/$429.00, down three dollars from Monday's late level. --Brian Spoors London Newsroom +44 171 542 8058
